title: Do My Teammates Trust Me?
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This reflective post asks readers to assess how much their colleagues actually trust them. It argues that trust is hard to measure because it accumulates from many small experiences, perceptions and judgments rather than from one attribute. The author distills what colleagues quietly evaluate into five questions covering competence, candor, reliability, respect and availability. The suggested exercise is honest self-assessment: answer each question as colleagues would, not as you hope they would. The piece closes on the reminder that trust is built slowly through kept promises, honest conversations and genuine attention.
points: Trust is a mosaic built over time, which is why it resists simple measurement.
Colleagues keep an informal ledger around five questions: competence, truthfulness, promise-keeping, respect and availability.
Making time for people is treated as a form of care that builds trust.
The five questions work as a self-audit, provided you answer as your colleagues would rather than as you wish.
Trust is earned slowly, lost quickly, and always rebuildable through small consistent acts.
quotes: Trust is one of the most powerful and elusive forces in any workplace. Without it, not much gets done. With more of it, great things happen.
What makes trust so hard to measure is its complexity. It isn’t built on a single moment or attribute, but rather on a mosaic of experiences, perceptions, and judgments accumulated over time.

Your colleagues aren’t consciously scoring you against a well-known rubric, but they are drawing conclusions, constantly and quietly, from everything they observe. These conclusions tend to cluster around five core questions your teammates ask themselves about you:
Do you tell me the truth? Your teammates gauge trust by judging how candid you are, especially when that honesty is uncomfortable.
Ask yourself candidly how your colleagues would answer each one. Not how you hope they would answer, but how they likely would based on their real experience with you.

Trust is earned slowly and lost quickly. But it is always within your power to build and rebuild. Trust is created one kept promise, one honest conversation, and one moment of genuine attention at a time.
